transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-04-01
Start: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees (recorded): Sofia Martinez, Ethan Cole, Priya Singh, Marcus Lee, Nina Alvarez, Rae Johnson, Tom Becker, Sanjay Rao + ~110 others on the all-hands line

Summary: Quick all-hands focused on runway, Q2 hiring constraints, and a short product pulse on Private offerings and reliability spending. Open Q&A at the end.

[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, uh, good morning. We're gonna kick off the Mosaic briefing — thanks for joining, lot of folks on. Quick agenda: runway, hiring, private deploy update, reliability, then Q&A. I'll try to keep us tight.

[00:28] Ethan Cole: Morning all — short note from me before we dig in. We're in a good product momentum spot but runway is tighter than we'd like. This is a working deck not a final legal doc, so take the numbers as directional.

[01:05] Marcus Lee: I'll take the budget slide. So current cash runway at plan A is about 10 months, that's without additional hiring freezes. We modeled two scenarios: conservative and growth. The conservative holds headcount flat, growth adds ~15 hires in Q2. The delta on runway is roughly three months.

[01:42] Marcus Lee: We also reforecast unit economics — token cost continues to decline on host providers but our Dedicated throughput spend is more fixed. There's an assumption that batching improvements from the runtime team save us 12% on variable spend starting Jun.

[02:20] Priya Singh: Quick question on the assumption: are we counting the planned caching improvements for Redwood Dedicated? I saw a note in the infra brief about prefix caching and some kernel changes. If those slip, the savings don't show up.

[02:48] Nina Alvarez: Yeah, the research team is running a micro-bench of the new kv-cache heuristics, but it's early. We have some noisy runs where latency regresses at long seq lengths, so we need more tuning.

[03:15] Sofia Martinez: Noted. Marcus, can you put a 10% sensitivity in the deck for caching delays so we can see the impact?

[03:28] Marcus Lee: Yep, I'll add that.

[03:40] Priya Singh: On hiring, our priority list is: (1) serving runtime engineers, (2) product infra for Private deployments, (3) SRE for SLAs. If we're trimming headcount, we ask to protect those roles. They're critical for the 2025 roadmaps.

[04:10] Rae Johnson: We are prioritizing reqs as requested; we've got a few offers out. Early data suggests the market for quant engineers is slow, but infra folks are moving faster.

[04:32] Tom Becker: On Private deployments — short pulse: the Private pilot with Org23 is active, we hit a couple of network / egress config snags. The VPC peering was misconfigured and that caused a throughput drop. We fixed with a routing rule but still need the on-prem agent update.

[05:05] Sofia Martinez: That's the agent that does the KMS handshake right?

[05:09] Tom Becker: Right, there's an HSM/KMS flow. One thing to call out is that the on-prem package naming got mangled in the build — some folks call it Redwood Private Agent, others the docker image is redwood-deci... or redwood-decide, the transcript generator will say weird things, but the actual artifact is redwood-private-agent:v0.9.

[05:42] [laughter / background] Speaker 7: (inaudible)

[06:05] Nina Alvarez: On reliability investments, we've prioritized three programs: observability retention, regional failover testing, and automatic fallback model routing. The goal is to push our 95th percentile latency down by 20% for hosted API customers by end of Q3.

[06:40] Marcus Lee: That comes with cost. We estimate observability retention increase to add $Xk per month; I put conservative and aggressive buckets in the deck.

[07:12] Priya Singh: For the fallback routing, we need SE time to validate model compat matrices. If the fallback triggers, we want graceful degradation not opaque errors. That's a product+SE cross-team effort.

[07:40] Sofia Martinez: We'll allocate two SEs for 6 weeks to set up the acceptance tests. Priya, can you propose names?

[07:55] Priya Singh: I'll send a shortlist after this.

[08:05] [12:00 marker omitted - jumps to product pulse]

[08:19] Sofia Martinez: Product pulse: small update on model catalog and experiments. We're leaning into a policy of 'verified performance profiles' — basically more explicit metadata about seq length costs and tail-latency on each model variant. Expect a new column in the console.

[08:46] Ethan Cole: This helps sales and solutions engineering set expectations — large customers ask for per-route SLOs and token cost estimates.

[09:02] Sanjay Rao: From sales side, having explicit perf profiles reduces the pre-sales benchmarking we do. If we can show per-model 95th latency numbers and recommended quantization for a given workload, that's gold.

[09:28] Sofia Martinez: We're also testing a tooling flow to auto-suggest batching and kv-cache config per-customer. That's part of Redwood Optimize work. It's still alpha.

[09:50] Nina Alvarez: Small note — the auto-suggest sometimes recommends larger batch sizes that increase tail latency for short-lived interactive sessions. We're adding heuristics for that.

[10:12] [10:30 approx - Finance Q&A]

[10:18] Marcus Lee: Quick Q&A on the numbers. Question in chat: what happens if we lose the top two pilot customers next quarter? We modeled that too — we'd need to pause non-essential hiring and pull back some calendar-driven expenditures. It's doable but painful.

[10:45] Ethan Cole: The strategy remains to prioritize product-market fit and high-leverage engineering work. We will not cut the core runtime team; instead we look at delaying some GTM hires if needed.

[11:00] Rae Johnson: Re hiring freeze rumors — we haven't moved to freeze, we're triaging requisitions. If there are changes, we'll post the org guidance in the handbook and notify managers.

[11:20] [12:00-30:00 condensed - skip long demos not recorded in detail]

[11:40] Sofia Martinez: Okay moving on to compliance — short update from Nina.

[11:45] Nina Alvarez: We're advancing SOC 2 Type II readiness. The compliance tracker shows three outstanding controls related to key lifecycle management and audit log retention. We need to finalize KMS rotation policy and increase log retention for the console. That will cost some additional storage and indexing.

[12:10] Marcus Lee: Add storage to the conservative bucket in the budget please. The storage line isn't huge but it is recurring.

[12:30] Priya Singh: On the technical side, the private deployment on-prem install script needs an idempotency pass. A failed install currently left leftover systemd units that required manual cleanup. We'll push a patch this week.

[12:48] Tom Becker: Also note some customers want FIPS-compliant build options; that's a longer lead item for on-prem. We'll catalog the ask and put it in the backlog.

[13:12] [15:00 mark - open Q&A. timestamps approximate.]

[13:20] All Hands Q: Any update on Dedicated reserved capacity pricing?

[13:25] Marcus Lee: We're exploring tiered committed discounts for longer commitments — 6/12/24 month buckets — to improve predictability for both customers and our capacity planning. There's some negotiation with cloud partners to get deeper discounts at scale.

[13:50] Staff Q: Will layoffs be needed?

[13:55] Ethan Cole: No layoffs planned today. We have to be disciplined on hiring and spend, but the leadership preference is to avoid people reductions. We'll manage spend via hiring cadence and non-headcount budgets first.

[14:20] Staff Q: What's the plan for Private to move from pilot to GA?

[14:30] Priya Singh: GA criteria: 1) stable on-prem agent releases with idempotent installer, 2) documented RBAC + audit logs + KMS integration, 3) guided rollout for first 5 customers and runbook for incident ops. We estimate GA readiness late Q3 if current velocity holds.

[14:55] Nina Alvarez: Add security certification baseline too; some enterprise customers require SOC 2 and network segmentation docs for GA.

[15:12] Sofia Martinez: Quick recap and next steps: Marcus publishes updated deck, Priya sends the Private GA roadmap, Rae updates hiring tracker, Nina finalizes compliance controls list. We'll do a follow-up product sync next Tuesday for owners.

[15:40] Marcus Lee: I'll try to have the condensed deck in the handbook by Thursday.

[15:50] Priya Singh: I'll send the rollout milestones and a risk matrix by Apr 15.

[16:05] Rae Johnson: Hiring tracker by Apr 6.

[16:20] Nina Alvarez: Compliance control updates by Apr 10.

[16:35] [closing] Ethan Cole: Thanks team, keep the questions coming in the #all-hands channel. We'll follow up with a short FAQ doc to address the most common ones.

[16:50] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone — meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: background noise and some cross talk during applause; a few product names transcribed oddly (redwood-deci... redwood-decide vs redwood-private-agent), some numbers (dollar amounts) were redacted by the recorder's confidence filter.
